title: What If You Got 1% Faster Every Time Someone Said Your Name?

lines.t: Leo! Breakfast!
lines.el: [shouting from downstairs] Leo! Breakfast!

lines.t: You blink. And you're already downstairs.
lines.el: You blink. And you're already downstairs.

lines.t: Your toast is still in the air. Your mom hasn't even finished saying your name.
lines.el: Your toast is still in the air. Your mom hasn't even finished saying your name.

lines.t: Because starting today... every time someone says your name, you get one percent faster.
lines.el: Because starting today... every time someone says your name, you get one percent faster.

lines.t: And one percent... adds up.
lines.el: [ominous] And one percent... adds up.

lines.t: Here's the rule. Every time anyone, anywhere, says your name out loud, your speed goes up by one percent. And every hour nobody says it... you lose one percent.
lines.el: Here's the rule. Every time anyone, anywhere, says your name out loud, your speed goes up by one percent. And every hour nobody says it... you lose one percent.

lines.t: Your top speed right now? Twenty four kilometers an hour. A normal fifteen year old.
lines.el: Your top speed right now? Twenty four kilometers an hour. A normal fifteen year old.

lines.t: But percentages stack. Sixty two times, and you're as fast as Usain Bolt.
lines.el: But percentages stack. Sixty two times, and you're as fast as Usain Bolt.

lines.t: Three hundred ninety six times. You break the speed of sound.
lines.el: Three hundred ninety six times. You break the speed of sound.

lines.t: And seventeen hundred seventy one times... you're running at the speed of light.
lines.el: And seventeen hundred seventy one times... you're running at the speed of light.

lines.t: That's fewer people than go to some schools.
lines.el: [pause] That's fewer people than go to some schools.

lines.t: Day one. The problem is... nobody really says your name.
lines.el: Day one. The problem is... nobody really says your name.

lines.t: You're the quiet kid. Back row. Headphones. On a good day, your name gets said maybe three times.
lines.el: You're the quiet kid. Back row. Headphones. On a good day, your name gets said maybe three times.

lines.t: Leo? ...Leo. Present?
lines.el: [bored] Leo? ...Leo. Present?

lines.t: Plus one. Plus one.
lines.el: Plus one. Plus one.

lines.t: So you get creative. A name tag. A loud hello to everyone in the hallway. You even join the basketball team, just so the coach yells at you.
lines.el: So you get creative. A name tag. A loud hello to everyone in the hallway. You even join the basketball team, just so the coach yells at you.

lines.t: LEO! Pass the ball! LEO!
lines.el: [yelling] LEO! Pass the ball! LEO!

lines.t: By Friday, you run the forty meter dash in three seconds flat. The coach drops his stopwatch.
lines.el: By Friday, you run the forty meter dash in three seconds flat. The coach drops his stopwatch.

lines.t: Then someone films you outrunning the school bus.
lines.el: Then someone films you outrunning the school bus.

lines.t: By morning, it has eleven million views. And every comment, every reaction video, every person telling their friend about you... says your name.
lines.el: [building] By morning, it has eleven million views. And every comment, every reaction video, every person telling their friend about you... says your name.

lines.t: Dude, did you see Leo?! Leo is insane!
lines.el: [excited] Dude, did you see Leo?! Leo is insane!

lines.t: Plus one percent. Plus one percent. Plus one percent. Faster than you can count.
lines.el: Plus one percent. Plus one percent. Plus one percent. Faster than you can count.

lines.t: At lunch, you stand up too fast. And the air around you cracks like thunder.
lines.el: [tense] At lunch, you stand up too fast. And the air around you cracks like thunder.

lines.t: A sonic boom. Every window in the cafeteria explodes at once.
lines.el: A sonic boom. Every window in the cafeteria explodes at once.

lines.t: Nobody's hurt. But for the first time... people are scared of you.
lines.el: Nobody's hurt. But for the first time... people are scared of you.

lines.t: Day four. Forty thousand kilometers an hour. Escape velocity. If you jumped right now, you would leave the Earth.
lines.el: Day four. Forty thousand kilometers an hour. Escape velocity. If you jumped right now, you would leave the Earth.

lines.t: You learn to move slowly. Painfully slowly. Every step has to be gentle, or you'll go through a wall.
lines.el: You learn to move slowly. Painfully slowly. Every step has to be gentle, or you'll go through a wall.

lines.t: And then something strange starts happening. To time.
lines.el: And then something strange starts happening. To time.

lines.t: Einstein figured this out over a hundred years ago. The faster you move, the slower your clock ticks compared to everyone else.
lines.el: Einstein figured this out over a hundred years ago. The faster you move, the slower your clock ticks compared to everyone else.

lines.t: At ninety nine point nine nine percent of light speed, one day for you... is seventy days for them.
lines.el: At ninety nine point nine nine percent of light speed, one day for you... is seventy days for them.

lines.t: You run to the store to buy milk. When you get home, it's two months later.
lines.el: [quietly] You run to the store to buy milk. When you get home, it's two months later.

lines.t: Leo? Leo! Where have you been?!
lines.el: [crying, relieved] Leo? Leo! Where have you been?!

lines.t: Every time she says it, you get faster. And every time you get faster... you lose her a little more.
lines.el: Every time she says it, you get faster. And every time you get faster... you lose her a little more.

lines.t: You do the math. If this keeps going, one afternoon for you will be ten years for your family. Your little sister Mia will grow up while you blink.
lines.el: You do the math. If this keeps going, one afternoon for you will be ten years for your family. Your little sister Mia will grow up while you blink.

lines.t: There's only one way to slow down.
lines.el: [serious] There's only one way to slow down.

lines.t: The world has to forget your name.
lines.el: The world has to forget your name.

lines.t: So you disappear. You delete everything. You ask everyone to stop talking about you. You stop going to school.
lines.el: So you disappear. You delete everything. You ask everyone to stop talking about you. You stop going to school.

lines.t: And slowly... the world moves on. The videos stop. The memes die. Nobody says Leo anymore.
lines.el: And slowly... the world moves on. The videos stop. The memes die. Nobody says Leo anymore.

lines.t: Minus one percent. Minus one percent. Every hour.
lines.el: Minus one percent. Minus one percent. Every hour.

lines.t: Light speed. Then rocket speed. Then a car. Then... just you. Normal. For one perfect afternoon, you're exactly as fast as everyone else.
lines.el: Light speed. Then rocket speed. Then a car. Then... just you. Normal. For one perfect afternoon, you're exactly as fast as everyone else.

lines.t: But the rule doesn't stop at normal.
lines.el: [ominous] But the rule doesn't stop at normal.

lines.t: After a week of silence, you're moving at one fifth speed. Your hand takes ten seconds to reach a glass of water.
lines.el: After a week of silence, you're moving at one fifth speed. Your hand takes ten seconds to reach a glass of water.

lines.t: After a month... you're a statue. To you, it feels like a slow blink. To everyone else, you haven't moved in days.
lines.el: After a month... you're a statue. To you, it feels like a slow blink. To everyone else, you haven't moved in days.

lines.t: You can hear the house around you. You just can't move.
lines.el: [whispers] You can hear the house around you. You just can't move.

lines.t: Your mom stops saying your name. Not because she forgot. Because it hurts too much.
lines.el: Your mom stops saying your name. Not because she forgot. Because it hurts too much.

lines.t: And then, one night... the door opens. It's Mia. She sits on the edge of your bed, the way she used to when she had nightmares.
lines.el: And then, one night... the door opens. It's Mia. She sits on the edge of your bed, the way she used to when she had nightmares.

lines.t: Leo.
lines.el: [softly] Leo.

lines.t: Plus one percent. Your finger twitches.
lines.el: Plus one percent. Your finger twitches.

lines.t: Leo. Leo. Leo!
lines.el: [tearful] Leo. Leo. Leo!

lines.t: She doesn't stop. She says it a hundred times. Then she comes back the next morning and says it again. And again. Every single day.
lines.el: [emotional] She doesn't stop. She says it a hundred times. Then she comes back the next morning and says it again. And again. Every single day.

lines.t: Not millions of strangers. Just one little girl who refuses to let you disappear.
lines.el: Not millions of strangers. Just one little girl who refuses to let you disappear.

lines.t: And for the first time, you understand. Your name was never about speed. It was about being remembered.
lines.el: And for the first time, you understand. Your name was never about speed. It was about being remembered.

lines.t: Morning, Leo.
lines.el: [smiling] Morning, Leo.

lines.t: A year later, you're normal again. Mia says your name every morning. Exactly one hundred times. No more, no less.
lines.el: A year later, you're normal again. Mia says your name every morning. Exactly one hundred times. No more, no less.

lines.t: And then, your phone buzzes.
lines.el: [pause] And then, your phone buzzes.

lines.t: Someone found the old video. It's trending again. Number one. Worldwide.
lines.el: Someone found the old video. It's trending again. Number one. Worldwide.

lines.t: And you feel your heartbeat... speeding up.
lines.el: [whispers] And you feel your heartbeat... speeding up.

lines.t: Would you want this power? And who would say your name every day? Tell me in the comments.
lines.el: Would you want this power? And who would say your name every day? Tell me in the comments.
